implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py – option 1 calls add_transaction(tracker, "expense") which creates a Transaction via BudgetTracker.add_transaction and saves it.
main.py – option 2 calls add_transaction(tracker, "income") which creates a Transaction of type "income".
main.py – option 3 calls print_transactions(tracker.transactions); reports.py defines print_transactions that formats and prints all stored Transaction objects.
main.py – option 4 calls delete_transaction which invokes BudgetTracker.remove_transaction(tid) and reports success/failure.
main.py – option 5 calls set_budget which uses BudgetTracker.set_budget to store a Budget object.
main.py – option 6 calls print_budgets(tracker); reports.py defines print_budgets that shows limit, spent, remaining and status.
main.py – option 7 calls print_summary(tracker); reports.py computes total income, total expense via tracker.total and savings via tracker.savings.
tracker.py – load() reads from storage.load_data(); save() writes via storage.save_data(). main.py calls tracker.load() at start and each mutating operation triggers save().

judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional command‑line budget tracker covering expense/income entry, transaction listing, deletion, budget limits per category, summary of totals and savings, and JSON persistence. All core features are present and the program appears ready to run without missing stubs or placeholder code, leading to a passing verdict.
